A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SLDBench and SLDAgent research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V2 reports original agent evaluations, law-fitting analyses, model-selection results, and ablations in Sections 4 and B.7, using experimental data collected from prior literature.

after.justification: V3 retains original evaluations and applications, revises benchmark results, and adds original non-monotonic extrapolation experiments in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The joint evolution of Expression and Optimization routines, program selection, multi-island search, and final-law selection remain unchanged. The new U-shaped law is an output discovered on an added task, rather than a revision to SLDAgent's algorithm.

E1.justification: V3 adds u_shape: 516 observations across nine easy-question benchmark groups, testing compute-to-Brier-score prediction where extrapolation encounters non-monotonic behavior. This substantially extends the represented scaling scenarios. The original seven tasks and downstream model-selection datasets remain.

E2.justification: Table 3 removes Grok-CLI/Grok-4, adds Gemini-CLI/Gemini-3-Pro and Claude Code/Claude-Haiku-4.5 comparisons, and replaces the Sonnet-4 pairing with Sonnet-4.5. The seven general-purpose agent families and five model-selection baselines are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes the reported common backbone from o4-mini to GPT-5, and provider-model settings are updated. Benchmark evaluation narrows from R2, NMSE, and NMAE to R2. Appendix E introduces log-compute preprocessing and group-specific extrapolation thresholds. However, Section 4.1 still describes o4-mini as the default, conflicting with the revised table.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a dedicated adversarial extrapolation analysis: fitting small-compute observations and testing subsequent non-monotonic behavior. Figure 5 compares polynomial failures with discovered-law predictions on three representative tasks. The original co-optimization ablation and iteration analysis remain unchanged, including the relocated Figure 4.

E5.justification: Main benchmark results are reported over five runs instead of three. V3 Table 5 extends R2 standard-deviation reporting to baseline agents, whereas v2 Tables 7–9 cover only SLDAgent variants. NMSE/NMAE uncertainty tables disappear. The retained ablation still reports three-run means.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 substantially revise reported scores; for example, SLDAgent/GPT-5's lr&bsz R2 changes from 0.610 to 0.955 alongside revised reporting settings. New u_shape results range from 0.838 to 0.931 for SLDAgent, versus approximately -950 for the polynomial baseline in Appendix E. NMSE/NMAE results are removed; application and ablation results are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix E introduces explicit mathematical definitions for the polynomial comparator and the discovered linear-plus-Gaussian law, including positivity constraints. The existing closed-form learning-rate/batch-size derivation is unchanged apart from numbering. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract is identical, and the introduction's contribution summary and conclusion retain the same central claims: SLDBench, evolutionary law-and-fitter optimization, superior extrapolation, and practical pretraining/fine-tuning utility. The additional experiments support these retained headline claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.5 distinguishes contamination threats and interprets SLDBench as literature-aware, qualifying what 'superhuman' performance establishes. Section 6 explicitly separates law discovery from variable discovery. Section 4.2 acknowledges ties and remaining model-capacity limitations, while Appendix E adds interpretations of non-monotonic extrapolation.

D1.justification: V3 adds dataset and leaderboard links, documents the Python 3.12-slim sandbox and network isolation, and states that split-regeneration code is provided. It supplies the new task's prompt, preprocessing, thresholds, and fitting details. Existing agent configurations, application code, and evolutionary budgets remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Wu and Lo (2024) for non-monotonic scaling and Jain et al. (2024), LiveCodeBench, for contamination-aware benchmark renewal. The existing related-work section and broad research positioning are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. V3 revises introductory and results-analysis paragraphs, adds targeted appendix sections, consolidates metric-reporting subsections, renames lr_and_bsz to lr&bsz, and edits author affiliations/order. These are localized changes rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with revised categories, labels, and legend; Tables 1–3 expand for the eighth task and updated comparisons. Several appendix metric tables are replaced by one broader uncertainty table. Appendix E adds two tables and a six-panel Figure 5, while retained Figure 4 moves beside its analysis.

improvement.justification: Baseline-wide uncertainty reporting and explicit contamination/applicability limits improve assessability. The non-monotonic study broadens validation, although its prompt supplies the expected curve shape. V3 also introduces an aggregation error: Tables 2–3 retain the old human average of 0.738 although their eight displayed entries average approximately 0.520. These reporting and interpretation weaknesses limit the overall gain.
